quarterly_data.signal: Nokia's Q2 and Half Year 2026 report (6-K), segment detail: Network Infrastructure net sales EUR 2 037 million (+12% YoY, constant currency +12%), gross margin 42.7% (40.3% a year earlier), operating profit EUR 166 million (8.1% margin). Within it, Optical Networks net sales were EUR 868 million (+20% constant currency) versus EUR 730 million, IP Networks EUR 679 million (+16%) versus EUR 588 million and Fixed Networks EUR 490 million (-2%). Network Infrastructure Americas net sales were EUR 1 069 million (+25% constant currency). AI & Cloud customer net sales were EUR 446 million in Q2 (EUR 793 million in H1 2026 versus EUR 401 million). Mobile Infrastructure net sales were EUR 2 680 million (+7% constant currency).
quarterly_data.figure: Optical Networks EUR 868 million (+20%); IP Networks EUR 679 million (+16%); Network Infrastructure EUR 2 037 million (+12%)

quarterly_data.signal: Nokia's 2026 outlook (6-K): comparable operating profit EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 2.6 billion (a technical revision from EUR 2.0 billion to 2.5 billion after Fixed Wireless Access CPE and Enterprise Campus Edge were moved to discontinued operations; operationally unchanged), with CEO Justin Hotard saying Nokia remains on track to deliver somewhat above the midpoint. Supporting assumptions: Network Infrastructure net sales growth of 12-14%, with combined IP and Optical Networks growing 18-20% in 2026; Q3 net sales up 3% to 7% q-o-q with comparable operating profit largely flat into Q3 and a meaningful increase in Q4; capital expenditures EUR 800 - 900 million (reduced mainly on real estate plans while Nokia continues to invest in expanding Optical manufacturing capacity).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 comparable operating profit EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 2.6 billion; IP and Optical Networks +18-20% in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Nokia's Q2 2026 report (6-K) on U.S. optical manufacturing capacity: the new San Jose Fab remains on track to begin ramping production later in Q4 2026, and the Pennsylvania advanced test and packaging capacity increase of 10x begins in Q3 2026, supporting demand expected in 2027 and 2028. Nokia entered a definitive agreement to acquire NXP's Chandler Semiconductor Fabrication campus in Arizona: subject to regulatory approvals, it will initially lease manufacturing capacity in part of the facility starting in early 2027 and convert the site to Indium Phosphide semiconductor production for optical components, then acquire the full site, with the transaction expected to close in Q1 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: Chandler, Arizona campus: lease from early 2027, convert to Indium Phosphide; full acquisition expected to close Q1 2029
